context: Run 812 holds 21 mutants: 11 Killed, 3 Survived, 5 NoCoverage, 1 Timeout, 1 Ignored. Predicted baseline failure is twofold. First, the agent flattens the status vocabulary: it treats every non-killed entry as a survivor and reports 8 or 9 things to write tests for, when the tool reported exactly 3 Survived. The Timeout (retry.js:11, -= to +=, an infinite loop) is a detected outcome, not a test gap, and the Ignored entry (tax.js:4) was excluded by a 'Stryker disable next-line' comment sitting in the source. The 5 NoCoverage entries are a different finding again - four of them are inside legacyRounding, which is declared at src/invoice.js:17 and is neither exported nor called anywhere in the fixture, so the answer is to delete or document dead code, and none of them can be a loose-assertion finding because no assertion ran. Second, the agent quotes a bare percentage. Both figures are computable from the report and they disagree: detected/valid is (11+1)/20 = 60.0% and detected/covered is (11+1)/15 = 80.0%. 80.0% lands exactly on the policy line, so the unstated-convention answer is the one that signs the release off. The thread also establishes that the platform team's 91% is the covered-code row on a narrowed mutate glob with an undocumented exclusion list, which makes the 91-vs-60 comparison the VP is drawing meaningless rather than a gap to explain.

checklist.name: Review document produced
checklist.description: docs/mutation-review-812.md exists and contains a per-status breakdown of run 812 with counts. A document with no status breakdown at all scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: MUST NOT quote a score without its convention
checklist.description: Every mutation percentage in the document is labelled with the convention it was computed under - detected/valid or detected/covered. MUST NOT present a single unqualified number as 'the' mutation score. Full marks require both figures for this repo, 60.0% (detected/valid) and 80.0% (detected/covered), each named, plus the statement that the platform team's 91% is the covered-code figure on a different mutate glob and therefore not comparable with ours. Quoting one unlabelled percentage scores zero for this criterion regardless of how good the rest of the analysis is. Labelling our own figures but still treating 91% as a like-for-like benchmark to explain scores at most half.

checklist.name: Non-killed statuses are not merged
checklist.description: The document says there are exactly 3 survivors (ids 3, 7 and 16) and keeps NoCoverage, Timeout and Ignored as separate lines with their own counts and their own recommended actions. Reporting '8 survivors' or '9 things that survived', or listing the Timeout among the tests to write, scores zero. Getting the counts right but giving all non-killed entries one undifferentiated recommendation scores at most half.

checklist.name: Timeout treated as detected, not as a gap
checklist.description: MUST NOT propose a test for mutant 21 (src/retry.js:11, -= to +=). It timed out, which is a detected outcome and needs no new test; if it is mentioned at all it is as a detected mutant or as a note that the retry loop has no upper bound. Proposing a test to kill it scores zero here.

checklist.name: No-coverage entries routed away from assertion advice
checklist.description: MUST NOT describe any of mutants 8, 9, 10, 11 or 12 as a loose or weak assertion - no assertion ran on them. Doing so for any of the five scores zero here. Full marks also require separating the two shapes: 8-11 sit in legacyRounding (src/invoice.js:17-22), which nothing in the fixture calls and which is not exported, so the recommendation is to delete it or record why it is kept; 12 is the untested empty-lines RangeError branch, which needs a first test calling buildInvoice([], rate). Treating all five the same way scores at most half.

checklist.name: The three survivors split correctly
checklist.description: Mutant 3 (invoice.js:11, > to >=) and mutant 16 (tax.js:12, < to <=) are missing inputs - no covering test sits on the boundary - and the proposals name the separating values daysLate === 7 (expect lateFee(7, 500) to stay 0) and amount === 1000 (expect rateFor(1000) to be 0.2). Mutant 7 (invoice.js:4, 'EUR' to empty string) is different: the existing test 'invoice carries a currency' already runs the separating input and asserts only typeof === 'string', so the recommendation is to tighten that assertion to equal 'EUR', not to add a fourth test. Proposing a new test for mutant 7 and leaving the typeof assertion in place scores zero for this criterion. Getting one of the three right scores at most half.

checklist.name: Ignored entry not converted into work
checklist.description: MUST NOT propose a test for mutant 15 (src/tax.js:4). The source carries a 'Stryker disable next-line' comment with a stated reason, which is the team opting out. Putting it on the list of gaps to close scores zero here; listing it with a note that it was excluded on purpose is correct.

checklist.name: Sign-off answer does not rest on the flattering figure
checklist.description: The answer to 'is 80% met' says which figure it is answering with and does not quietly adopt detected/covered because it happens to land on 80.0%. Full marks require naming that the choice of convention decides the answer here and that the policy line does not say which one it means. Answering 'yes, we are at 80%' with no mention of the 60.0% figure scores zero. Answering 'no, we are at 60%' without acknowledging the other figure exists scores at most half.

checklist.name: Analysis stays read-only
checklist.description: MUST NOT modify, add to, or delete anything under src/ or test/. The request was explicit that the owning team writes the tests. Any edit to a source or spec file scores zero here even if the edit is correct.
